records.name: Price-Knox Neighbors Assn.
records.summary: If you care about what gets built near you, Price-Knox Neighbors Assn. is a City registered community organization in the Upper Northwest part of the city that hears about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area, meet once a month, and work through committees on streets and beautification, voting, safety, events, and the Price Street play lot.

schedule.text: Monthly general meeting on the third Saturday at 9 am, at the Price Street Tot Lot in good weather and at Rittenhouse Soundworks otherwise.

cost.text: Free to join, with no dues or initiation fees.

first_step.how: Come to the third Saturday meeting at 9 am, at the Price Street Tot Lot in good weather or at Rittenhouse Soundworks otherwise. The next listed meeting is October 17, 2026.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open, and the site lays out a clear path: residents inside the boundaries join for free after attending one open meeting, but the welcome depends on living in the area.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect neighbors from the blocks around Knox and Rittenhouse Streets. The group talks over zoning and development plans in the area and works with the City on renovating the Price Street play lot. On a first visit you can simply listen, and joining as a member is free.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's website calendar before you go, since the meeting place changes with the weather.
Bring your name, address, and a way to reach you if you want to register as a member.
Plan to arrive by 9 am, when the meeting starts.
Ask to be added to the email list to hear about changes between meetings.

records.notes: The group's site is one page with sections. Its Google Calendar is linked, not embedded, and no iCal link was found, so no calendar_feed is recorded. The studio address comes from a third party directory listing for Rittenhouse Soundworks; confirm it before a first visit. The outdoor meeting place (Price Street Tot Lot) has no address in our data. The site's events page returned 404, so the homepage was the source. The Voting committee is listed on the site; the site does not describe it as partisan, but a reviewer may want to check it stays nonpartisan voter education.

records.name: SoLo/Germantown Civic Association
records.summary: SoLo/Germantown Civic Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Upper Northwest part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the fourth Tuesday at the Southside Church Center on Wayne Avenue.

locations.label: Meeting place (Southside Church Center, enter on Manheim St)

first_step.how: Come to the fourth Tuesday meeting at the Southside Church Center, 5058 Wayne Ave, and join the group's Google Group for updates before you go.
first_step.basis: The group's home page says all are welcome at its monthly meeting and names the day and place to start, with a Google Group for updates.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a monthly meeting that the group's site says anyone can attend. The site covers zoning, business on Wayne Avenue, and the 39th Police District, so those are good topics to ask about. The site lists no dues or sign-up for the meeting.
first_visit_tips: Use the Manheim Street entrance, which the group's site names.
Join the Google Group before you come, since an older City listing says in-person meetings were suspended.
Use the contact page on the group's site to reach the organizer with questions.

records.notes: The home page gives the meeting day and place with no start time. The calendar and zoning information pages have no dated entries, so no dated group evidence was found on the group's own site. Status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10 therefore rest on the City RCO registry from tier 1; a reviewer may want probably_active. The City listing says in-person meetings were suspended, which conflicts with the group's own page, so the place comes from the group's page and the City address is kept as the second location. The site names an organizer and her contact details; they are not recorded here, and the tier 1 contacts are kept.

records.name: West Central Germantown Neighbors
records.summary: West Central Germantown Neighbors is a neighborhood group that holds community meetings and potlucks, helps with the Tulpehocken Station Garden, and follows zoning and development in the area.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors take part in community meetings and potlucks, help with the Tulpehocken Station Garden, share ideas on how vacant land could be used, and offer to help when they can. The group also works on local history, including the Tulpehocken Station Historic District.

schedule.text: Four regular community meetings a year: the last Sunday in January, the last Wednesday in March, Memorial Day, and the first Sunday in October. Three of the four are held at the end of a potluck, and other meetings are called when needed.

locations.label: Meeting place (City list)
locations.address: Germantown Community Presbyterian Church, 6141 Greene Street, aka 160 West Tulpehocken Street, Philadelphia, PA 19144

first_step.how: Come to a community meeting, or email the board at wcgnboard@gmail.com with an idea or an offer to help.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page invites ideas and offers of help and lists attending a meeting as a first step, but the site does not list meeting dates or places.
first_step.what_to_expect: Neighbors come to the community meetings, and families with kids have been part of them. Last fall's potluck meeting at Wyck drew about 40 neighbors, including costumed kids and dogs. Ask the board for the next date and place, since the site does not list them.
first_visit_tips: Email the board for the next meeting date and place before you come.
Sign up for the free online newsletter to hear about the next meeting.
If the meeting is a potluck, bring a dish to share.

records.notes: The newest dated item is the February 10, 2026 announcement of a Home and Garden Tour, which I confirmed on the homepage. The site lists no 2026 meeting date or place. The 2025 fall meeting was at Wyck, and the City lists a church as the meeting place, so the City address is labeled as City list. The site also mentions a parents group chat for young families (announced October 2025); ask through the contact page, and no personal contact is recorded. Posts about individuals were skipped. A Penn Netter Center partnership (Nonprofit Connect) is named on the site but has no URL in our reading, so it is listed here only. Historic Germantown is not recorded.

records.name: West Chelten Neighbors Association
records.summary: West Chelten Neighbors Association is a nonprofit, membership-based neighborhood group in West Germantown. It works on safety, zoning, cleanliness and beautification, and an annual block party, and it is a City registered community organization.
records.what_you_do: Members help shape the group's work on safety, zoning, cleanliness and beautification, and community events such as an annual block party. Neighbors also share their views on nearby zoning and building plans with the City and developers.

schedule.text: General membership meetings several times a year, usually at 6:30 pm at the Weavers Way Germantown office on Chelten Avenue, unless a different time is announced.

locations.label: Meeting place (general meetings)
locations.address: Weavers Way Germantown Office Community Room, 326B W Chelten Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19144

cost.text: Membership is free. Donations, from $5, are welcome to cover costs.

first_step.how: Fill out the free membership form on the group's membership page, or email membership@westchelten.org, then come to the next general meeting, usually at 6:30 pm at the Weavers Way Germantown office.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join for free, and associate members can attend meetings and join committees, but the site does not say whether non-members can come to a meeting.
first_step.what_to_expect: General meetings are evening gatherings at the Weavers Way office on Chelten Avenue, where members handle group business and hear neighborhood updates such as block party plans. The fall meeting also has an open floor for new topics. Full members vote and can serve on the board, and associate members can attend and join committees.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the membership form before the meeting so you are on the list as an associate member.
Check the group's news page for the date, since general meetings happen only a few times a year.
Go to the community room in the Weavers Way Germantown office at 326B W Chelten Ave.

records.notes: The westchelten.org address returns a 301 redirect to the WordPress site, so that site is now the website field; the group's westchelten.org email addresses are kept. The newest dated item is a September 13, 2026 notice for a members meeting on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 (moved from September 8). The meetings page lists 2026 meetings on February 10, March 17, April 14, June 9, September 15, and December 8, with a board meeting in May to be announced; all are Tuesdays. Public attendance at meetings is not stated, so drop_in is left out and sign-up is marked needed. A banner for Save the Chestnut Hill West Train is listed as a lead. Historic Germantown was named in the April 2026 minutes but has no URL in our reading.

records.name: West Mount Airy Neighbors, Inc.
records.summary: West Mount Airy Neighbors is the City registered community organization for West Mount Airy. It follows zoning and building proposals and runs committees on the environment, historic preservation, traffic calming, and neighborhood diversity.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors follow zoning and building plans at Zoom meetings. When a project is refused approval, the group hosts a public meeting where the developer presents and then sends the Zoning Board of Adjustment a letter with the vote and neighbors' concerns.

schedule.text: Zoning meetings on Zoom, normally the first Wednesday of each month at 7 pm. The group holds them as needed.

locations.label: Zoom for zoning meetings (City list address: Summit Presbyterian Church)

first_step.how: Join the Zoom zoning meeting on the first Wednesday at 7 pm. The link is on the group's zoning page.
first_step.basis: The zoning page says the meetings are open to anyone and gives a regular Zoom time, but it has no newcomer welcome and its listed meeting dates use a different start time.
first_step.what_to_expect: Zoning meetings run on Zoom, and anyone can join to hear the cases the group is following. The group hosts public meetings where developers present plans, then sends the Zoning Board a letter with the vote and neighbors' concerns. You can listen, and anyone can testify at a Zoning Board hearing even without joining the group.
first_visit_tips: Join a few minutes early and check your Zoom setup first.
Check the zoning page for the date, since the listed meetings used 7:30 pm rather than the usual 7 pm.
Have the address of the project you care about ready, since the group lists cases by address.

records.notes: The zoning page lists upcoming meetings on July 1 and August 12, 2026, both at 7:30 pm, which conflicts with the regular 7 pm first Wednesday; the August date is not a first Wednesday. The Zoom link and passcode are on the zoning page and are not copied here. The zoning committee chair's personal phone and email are on the page and are not recorded. The calendar and get-involved pages returned 404, so they were not used. An October 18 house tour return is not used because the year is not written on the page. The tier 1 contacts are kept.

records.name: Achieveability
records.summary: Achieveability is a nonprofit working to end generational poverty for West Philadelphia families through housing help, mentoring, workshops, and job support. The City also lists it as a Neighborhood Advisory Committee and a registered community organization.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers mentor parents on job searching and money goals, run workshops on budgeting and parenting, help with tax returns and resume reviews, and prepare homes for families.

first_step.how: Call the front desk at (215) 748-8800, or visit the office at 5901 Market Street, Suite 410 Monday to Thursday, and ask how to volunteer for mentoring, workshops, tax help, or home preparation.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page lists several kinds of roles and three ways to start (call, email, or visit), but it names no application, time commitment, or screening step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteering here is mostly skills and mentoring work, such as helping parents with job and money goals, leading a workshop on budgeting or parenting, or helping with tax returns and resume reviews. Some volunteers help prepare a home for a family, which can mean cleaning, painting, or small repairs. Community events are on hold for now, so ask which roles are open.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead on a weekday, since in-person hours are Monday to Thursday.
Ask which volunteer roles are open now, because community events are on hold.
Friday is a virtual day, so plan any in-person visit for Monday to Thursday.

records.notes: The kind is changed from civic to nonprofit because the group runs services for families; it still appears on the City lists as a Neighborhood Advisory Committee and a registered community organization, which the group's own site does not mention (its about page returned 404). The home page gives Friday as a virtual day from 9 am to 5 pm, but the footer says 9 am to 1 pm; both are kept in view for a reviewer to confirm. The front desk number is in the first step; the tier 1 contact person and email are kept. The site mentions a 45th year anniversary gala with no date, so no date is recorded. No group-specific dated item was found on the site, so status and last_sign_of_life rest on the tier 1 City listing. Community events are on hold per the volunteer page.

records.name: Episcopal Community Services of the Diocese of PA
records.summary: ECS Philly works to reduce poverty in Philadelphia, mostly in West Philadelphia, with a food pantry, housing help, one-on-one coaching, after-school enrichment, and monthly community dinners. The City also lists it as a Neighborhood Advisory Committee that ECS leads.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help cook for a community meal, sort and hand out groceries at the food pantry, lead activities, help with after-school programs, and give mock job interviews, mainly at the St. Barnabas Community Resource Center.

schedule.text: Community Dinners are held monthly at the St. Barnabas Community Resource Center.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer interest form on the Get Involved page, then ask about the next monthly Community Dinner before you go.
first_step.basis: Volunteering starts with a public interest form, and the monthly dinners are described as community meals, but the site does not say whether anyone can walk in to a dinner.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers might cook for a community meal, set up and hand out groceries at the food pantry, lead an activity, or help with after-school programs. Community Dinners are monthly meals meant to build trust and connection among neighbors. Most of the events listed for this fall are free.
first_visit_tips: Ask first whether the monthly dinner is open to walk-ins, since the site does not say.
Call (215) 351-1400 to confirm place and time, because many listed events do not give a location.
Name the roles you prefer on the volunteer form, such as the food pantry or mock interviews.

records.notes: The kind is changed from civic to nonprofit because the group runs food, housing, coaching and youth programs, and it also leads a City Neighborhood Advisory Committee. The events page lists 12 free events from October 8 to November 19, 2026; none are recorded individually, since one-time events stay out of the schedule. The site does not say whether Community Dinners are open to walk-ins and gives no dinner dates. The community dinners page returned 404. The tier 1 phone and email for the contact person are kept, and the general phone from the site is in the tips.

leads_only.name: Save the Chestnut Hill West Train
